# Modernize the Systems Your Business Runs On
Legacy systems raise costs, slow delivery and block AI. Publicis Sapient combines enterprise experts with AI platforms to modernize them without putting live operations at risk.
[](https://www.publicissapient.com/platforms/slingshot/legacy-modernization)[](https://www.publicissapient.com/contact)
## What makes modernization hard
We've spent decades inside these systems. These are the problems that come up in nearly every enterprise.
### Legacy tech can’t keep up with change
<p>Core systems are costly, tightly linked and hard to update. Embedded business logic and technical debt slow every change and raise operational risk.</p>
### Operations don’t work as one system
<p>Supply chains, fulfillment, field operations and partner networks still run across disconnected platforms and manual workflows.</p>
### Digital can’t move at customer speed
<p>Aging platforms and fragmented delivery models make it harder to improve products, launch services and respond to changing customer needs.</p>
### Transformation can’t disrupt the business
<p>Critical systems must keep running while they change. Every modernization plan must protect customers, employees and day-to-day operations.</p>

## Enterprise modernization FAQS
What is enterprise modernization?
Enterprise modernization is the work of updating legacy applications, data, infrastructure and delivery practices so the business can change faster, carry less risk and support AI. It covers the systems themselves and the way teams build and run them.
How is modernization different from a system migration?
A migration moves a system to a new environment. Modernization changes the system itself—its architecture, code, data and workflows—while preserving the business logic it still depends on. A migration can leave you with the same constraints in a newer place.
How do you modernize without disrupting operations?
The work starts by mapping dependencies, business rules and live workflows. Teams then modernize in controlled stages, validating each change against how the original system behaves before anything switches over, so critical systems keep running throughout.
